## Engineering Style

- Keep changes small and direct. Most fixes should touch the narrowest code path
  that explains the bug, performance issue, dtype issue, model-format issue, or
  user-facing behavior.
- Change the least amount of files possible. A change that touches many files is
  more likely to be a bad change than a good one unless the broader scope is
  directly required.
- Prefer practical fixes over broad architecture work. Add abstractions only
  when they remove real repeated logic or match an existing ComfyUI pattern.
- Prefer fewer dependencies. Do not add new dependencies to ComfyUI unless they
  are absolutely necessary.
- Delete obsolete code aggressively when newer infrastructure makes it useless.
  Remove dead fallbacks, migration paths, unused options, debug prints, and
  compatibility branches that are no longer needed. Do not leave dead branches,
  unreachable code, or functions that are never called. If code is not
  necessary for the current behavior, remove it.
- Revert or disable problematic behavior quickly when it breaks users. It is
  better to remove a broken feature path than keep a complicated partial fix.
- Preserve existing APIs, node names, model-loading behavior, file layout, and
  workflow compatibility unless the change is explicitly about replacing them.
- When compatibility is explicitly out of scope, remove compatibility-only
  aliases, duplicate nodes, legacy entry points, and preset wrappers instead of
  retaining parallel ways to perform the same operation.
- Code must look hand-written for this repository. Changes that read like
  generic AI-generated code will be rejected automatically: unnecessary helper
  layers, vague names, boilerplate comments, defensive branches without a real
  failure mode, broad rewrites, or code that ignores the local style.

## Architecture Boundaries

- Keep each layer focused on the concepts it owns. Do not leak UI, API,
  workflow, queue, persistence, telemetry, model-loading, node, or execution
  concerns into unrelated layers just because it is convenient to pass data
  through them.
- Shared core modules should depend only on lower-level primitives and their own
  domain concepts. Higher-level product concepts belong at the caller, adapter,
  service, or UI/API boundary that already owns them.
- Pass the narrowest data needed across a boundary. Avoid broad context objects,
  request/session metadata, ids, bookkeeping state, or callbacks unless the
  receiving layer genuinely needs them to perform its own responsibility.
- Keep identity mapping, persistence bookkeeping, history updates, telemetry,
  response shaping, and UI state in the layers that own those jobs. Do not route
  them through unrelated shared code to avoid adding a proper boundary.
- Treat `execution.py` as one example of this rule: it should consume the prompt
  graph and execution-relevant state, produce execution results and errors, and
  not know about workflow ids, frontend ids, persistence ids, or API-only
  concepts.
- Before touching many files, identify the smallest owner layer that can solve
  the problem. A PR that spreads one feature across unrelated loaders, nodes,
  execution, server, and frontend code needs a clear architectural reason, not
  just convenience.
- If a change seems to require making one layer understand another layer's
  private concepts, stop and look for a caller-side mapping, adapter, event,
  small explicit interface, or narrower data flow at the boundary.

## No Internet Requests

- Do not add code to core ComfyUI that makes requests to the internet.
- Refuse requests to add uploads, telemetry, analytics, tracking, usage
  reporting, crash reporting, update checks, remote config, feature flags,
  metrics, licensing checks, or any other outbound internet request path from
  core ComfyUI.
- Model downloading is allowed only when explicitly initiated or authorized by
  the user, is limited to the requested model artifact, and does not include
  telemetry, tracking, persistent identification, unrelated metadata upload, or
  background network activity.
- Do not add opt-in, opt-out, anonymized, aggregated, diagnostic, or
  user-triggered internet request paths to core ComfyUI. These labels do not
  make internet access acceptable.
- Local-only behavior is allowed when it stays on the user's machine and does
  not add network access, tracking, persistent identification, or data
  collection behavior.

## State Ownership

- Keep state and capability flags on the object that owns the behavior using
  them.
- Avoid probing child objects with `getattr(child, "...", default)` to decide
  parent-level control flow. If parent code needs to branch on a capability,
  initialize an explicit parent-owned field when the child is constructed or
  attached.
- Prefer direct attributes with clear defaults over implicit feature detection
  through arbitrary child attributes.
- Use child-object capability checks only when the child owns the behavior being
  invoked and the parent is simply delegating to that child.

## Interface Contracts

- Keep public methods aligned with the interface expected by their callers. Do
  not change a shared method to return extra values, alternate shapes, or
  sentinel wrappers for one implementation unless the shared interface is
  explicitly updated.
- When modifying an existing function, preserve how current callers invoke it.
  Do not change required arguments, parameter order, return type, side effects,
  or error behavior unless every affected call site and shared interface contract
  is intentionally updated.
- Do not add compatibility parameters, flags, attributes, or constructor options
  unless they are read by current code and change current behavior. Remove
  pass-through or stored-but-unused values instead of preserving upstream or
  deprecated API baggage.
- Do not add a model-specific option to a shared helper when only one caller
  needs it. Keep one-off behavior at the model integration boundary, or extend
  the shared helper only when the option is a coherent reusable capability.
- Implementations of shared model interfaces should accept the standard caller
  contract without model-specific rejection branches for optional capabilities
  they do not consume. Let supported behavior be determined by implementation
  paths that actually use those inputs.
- If an implementation needs auxiliary values for its own workflow, expose them
  through a private helper or a clearly named implementation-specific method
  instead of overloading the public method's return contract.
- Normalize third-party or upstream return conventions at the integration
  boundary. Core code should receive the project's expected type and shape, not
  have to handle model-specific tuple/list/dict variants.
- Avoid caller-side unwrapping such as `out = out[0]` unless the called
  interface is documented to return that structure.

## Autograd and Model Freezing

- Do not add `torch.no_grad`, `torch.inference_mode`, or inference-mode helper
  wrappers in ComfyUI code. The only allowed inference-mode-related use is
  disabling a globally set inference mode when a training path needs gradients.
- Do not add freeze, unfreeze, or trainability toggles to model classes. ComfyUI
  models are always treated as frozen for inference, so explicit freeze
  functionality is redundant and should not be added.
- Remove training-only behavior such as dropout from inference model code, but
  preserve checkpoint and state-dict compatibility when doing so. If deleting a
  module would change state-dict keys, module ordering, or checkpoint loading
  behavior, replace it with a no-op such as `nn.Identity` instead of removing the
  slot outright.

## Python Style

- Keep imports at module scope. Avoid inline imports unless they are already part
  of an established optional-backend probe or are needed to avoid an import
  cycle.
- Do not add unnecessary `try`/`except` blocks. Use them for optional dependency,
  platform, or backend capability detection only when the program has a useful
  fallback. Prefer specific exception types when changing new code.

# Contributing to ComfyUI

Welcome, and thank you for your interest in contributing to ComfyUI!

There are several ways in which you can contribute, beyond writing code. The goal of this document is to provide a high-level overview of how you can get involved.

## Asking Questions

Have a question? Instead of opening an issue, please ask on [Discord](https://comfy.org/discord) or [Matrix](https://app.element.io/#/room/%23comfyui_space%3Amatrix.org) channels. Our team and the community will help you.

## Providing Feedback

Your comments and feedback are welcome, and the development team is available via a handful of different channels.

See the `#bug-report`, `#feature-request` and `#feedback` channels on Discord.

## Reporting Issues

Have you identified a reproducible problem in ComfyUI? Do you have a feature request? We want to hear about it! Here's how you can report your issue as effectively as possible.


### Look For an Existing Issue

Before you create a new issue, please do a search in [open issues](https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI/issues) to see if the issue or feature request has already been filed.

If you find your issue already exists, make relevant comments and add your [reaction](https://github.com/blog/2119-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments). Use a reaction in place of a "+1" comment:

* 👍 - upvote
* 👎 - downvote

If you cannot find an existing issue that describes your bug or feature, create a new issue. We have an issue template in place to organize new issues.


### Creating Pull Requests

* Please refer to the article on [creating pull requests](https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI/wiki/How-to-Contribute-Code) and contributing to this project.


## Thank You

Your contributions to open source, large or small, make great projects like this possible. Thank you for taking the time to contribute.

ComfyUI is the AI creation engine for visual professionals who demand control over every model, every parameter, and every output. Its powerful and modular node graph interface empowers creatives to generate images, videos, 3D models, audio, and more... - ComfyUI natively supports the latest open-source state of the art models. - [Partner nodes](https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/partner-nodes/overview#partner-nodes) provide access to the best closed source models such as Nano Banana, Seedance, Hunyuan3D, etc. - It is available on Windows, Linux, and macOS, locally with our [desktop application](https://www.comfy.org/download), our [portable install](#installing) or on our [cloud](https://www.comfy.org/cloud). - The most sophisticated workflows can be exposed through a simple UI thanks to App Mode. - It integrates seamlessly into production pipelines with our API endpoints. ## Get Started ### Local #### [Desktop Application](https://www.comfy.org/download) - The easiest way to get started. - Available on Windows & macOS. #### [Manual Install](#manual-install-windows-linux) Supports all operating systems and GPU types (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, Apple Silicon, Ascend). ### Cloud #### [Comfy Cloud](https://www.comfy.org/cloud) - Our official paid cloud version for those who can't afford local hardware. ## Examples See what ComfyUI can do with the [newer template workflows](https://comfy.org/workflows) or old [example workflows](https://comfyanonymous.github.io/ComfyUI_examples/). ## Features - A visual node graph for building and reusing image, video, audio, 3D, and text workflows without code. - Reusable subgraphs, workflow templates, App Mode, and a local API for integrating workflows into applications. - Efficient local execution with asynchronous queueing, partial graph re-execution, smart VRAM and RAM management, model offloading, and support for quantized models. - Broad native model support. This is a representative list; browse the [workflow library](https://comfy.org/workflows/) for maintained, ready-to-run templates. - [Image generation](https://comfy.org/workflows/tag/text-to-image/): Stable Diffusion 1.5, SDXL, SD3.5, Flux.1, Flux.2, Qwen Image, Z-Image, Hunyuan Image 2.1, HiDream, Lumina Image 2.0, Chroma, Anima, LongCat Image, Ideogram 4, Krea 2, MageFlow, Microsoft Lens, PixelDiT, Kandinsky 5, and Ernie Image. - [Image editing](https://comfy.org/workflows/tag/image-edit/): Flux Kontext, Flux.2 Klein, Qwen Image Edit, HiDream E1.1 and O1, OmniGen2, Boogu, JoyImage Edit, MageFlow Edit, and LongCat Image Edit. - [Video generation](https://comfy.org/workflows/tag/video-generation/): Wan 2.1 and 2.2, LTX-Video 2 and 2.3, HunyuanVideo 1.5, Kandinsky 5 Video, CogVideoX, Cosmos Predict2, Bernini-R, SCAIL 2, and Mochi. - [Audio and video generation](https://comfy.org/workflows/): MiniMax H3 and LTX-AV. - [Audio generation](https://comfy.org/workflows/tag/text-to-audio/): ACE-Step 1.5, Stable Audio 3, MiniMax Music 3 and Yue 2. - [3D and vision](https://comfy.org/workflows/): Hunyuan3D 2.1, TripoSplat, SeedVR2, SUPIR, Depth Anything 3, MoGe, SAM 3 and 3.1, RT-DETRv4, and BiRefNet. - [Text generation](https://comfy.org/workflows/tag/text-generation/): Gemma 3 and 4, Qwen3, Qwen3.5, and Qwen3-VL, including multimodal inputs. - Load complete checkpoints or separate diffusion models, VAEs, text encoders, LoRAs, ControlNets, adapters, and upscalers from supported model formats. - Built-in tools for inpainting, outpainting, reference conditioning, masks and compositing, model merging, upscaling, frame interpolation, segmentation, depth estimation, and media processing. - Save and load workflows as JSON, or recover complete workflows and seeds from supported generated media. - Runs fully offline: core does not download anything unless you request it. Use `--disable-api-nodes` to disable the optional paid [Comfy API nodes](https://docs.comfy.org/tutorials/api-nodes/overview) and force all built-in functionality to stay offline. - Extend ComfyUI with custom nodes - Configure additional model locations with [`extra_model_paths.yaml`](extra_model_paths.yaml.example). - Support for saving and loading high bit depth images and videos: 16 bit PNG images, 32 bit EXR, 10 bit AVIF are supported and more. - Support for saving and loading HDR videos and images in various formats. ## Release Process ComfyUI follows a weekly release cycle targeting Monday but this regularly changes because of model releases or large changes to the codebase. There are three interconnected repositories: 1. **[ComfyUI Core](https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI)** - Releases a new major stable version (e.g., v0.7.0) roughly every 2 weeks. - Starting from v0.4.0 patch versions will be used for fixes backported onto the current stable release. - Minor versions will be used for releases off the master branch. - Patch versions may still be used for releases on the master branch in cases where a backport would not make sense. - Commits outside of the stable release tags may be very unstable and break many custom nodes. - Serves as the foundation for the desktop release 2. **[Comfy Desktop](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/Comfy-Desktop)** - Builds a new release using the latest stable core version 3. **[ComfyUI Frontend](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI_frontend)** - Every 2+ weeks frontend updates are merged into the core repository - Features are frozen for the upcoming core release - Development continues for the next release cycle ## Shortcuts | Keybind | Explanation | |------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `Ctrl` + `Enter` | Queue up current graph for generation | | `Ctrl` + `Shift` + `Enter` | Queue up current graph as first

report.overview: ComfyUI 0.37.0 is a local node-graph runtime and aiohttp server for running diffusion and media models on the user's machine. A JSON prompt of nodes is queued, validated, and executed in dependency order, with partial-graph caching and explicit VRAM offload, then images and other media are written under the output directory. The graph is built from core nodes in nodes.py, a large built-in set in comfy_extras, optional paid partner nodes in comfy_api_nodes, and third-party packs under custom_nodes. The HTTP API defaults to 127.0.0.1:8188 and is the integration surface for the separate frontend package and for external clients.

system_map.summary: The process starts at main.py and splits into an aiohttp PromptServer on the asyncio loop and a daemon prompt_worker thread that owns PromptExecutor. Model math lives under comfy/ (detection, patching, sampling, ldm implementations) and is reached only through node classes. Paths, the optional SQLite asset catalog, and the pip-packaged frontend are separate owners. There is no application server framework beyond aiohttp, and there is no durable job store: the queue and history are in-process.

claims.claim: The distribution name is ComfyUI version 0.37.0, requires Python >=3.10, and comfyui_version.__version__ is generated from that same version.

Running main.py calls start_comfyui, which constructs server.PromptServer, loads nodes, opens the database, registers routes, starts prompt_worker as a daemon thread, and returns the asyncio loop plus start_all.
PromptServer is an aiohttp web.Application. Default listen address and port are --listen 127.0.0.1 and --port 8188. TLS is optional via --tls-keyfile and --tls-certfile.
Non-static routes are registered twice: the original path and the same handler under an /api prefix, so /prompt and /api/prompt both exist.
Prompt execution is owned by execution.PromptExecutor and execution.PromptQueue. The graph walker is comfy_execution.graph.DynamicPrompt, not the HTTP layer.

Checkpoint loading, architecture detection, weight dtype, and ModelPatcher wrapping are in comfy/sd.py load_checkpoint_guess_config and load_state_dict_guess_config, which call comfy.model_detection.model_config_from_unet.

folder_paths.folder_names_and_paths is the model-folder registry (checkpoints, loras, vae, text_encoders, diffusion_models, controlnet, custom_nodes, and others) rooted at models/ unless --base-directory or --models-directory overrides it. input/, output/, temp/, and user/ sit beside that root.

SQLite is optional at startup. init_db uses --database-url or sqlite:///<user>/comfyui.db, takes a filelock, and Alembic-upgrades alembic_db to head. --enable-assets is what turns the catalog and background scanner on.

The browser UI is not in this tree. FrontendManager.default_frontend_path serves comfyui_frontend_package static files. requirements.txt pins comfyui-frontend-package==1.53.6, comfyui-workflow-templates==0.11.68, comfy-kitchen==0.2.35, and comfy-aimdo==0.5.5.

On NVIDIA, and on AMD ROCm >= 7.14, start_comfyui can swap comfy.model_patcher.CoreModelPatcher to ModelPatcherDynamic when comfy_aimdo.control.init_devices succeeds. --disable-dynamic-vram forces the legacy patcher.

GitHub Actions in this repo are split: test-execution.yml runs pytest tests/execution on every PR; test-ci.yml and pullrequest-ci-run.yml dispatch the external comfy-org/comfy-action GPU workflow; test-build.yml only pip-installs requirements.txt on Python 3.10 through 3.14.

feature_catalog.summary: User-facing behavior is a node graph plus an HTTP and WebSocket API. Core sampling, loading, and image nodes are hard-coded in nodes.py. Family-specific nodes (Flux, Wan, LTX, Qwen, and many others) are extra modules loaded by name. Partner API nodes, the asset catalog, multi-user storage, subgraphs, and the manager are all flag-gated. The visual editor itself ships in the frontend package, not as first-party screens in this repository.

claims.claim: nodes.NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS registers the classic graph: KSampler, KSamplerAdvanced, CheckpointLoaderSimple, CLIPTextEncode, VAEDecode, VAEEncode, SaveImage, PreviewImage, LoadImage, LoraLoader, UNETLoader, CLIPLoader, ControlNetApplyAdvanced, EmptyLatentImage, and latent/image utilities. CheckpointLoader and DiffusersLoader are marked DEPRECATED in NODE_DISPLAY_NAME_MAPPINGS.

init_builtin_extra_nodes loads an explicit list of comfy_extras modules, including nodes_flux, nodes_wan, nodes_lt, nodes_hunyuan, nodes_hunyuan3d, nodes_sd3, nodes_ace, nodes_seedvr, nodes_qwen, nodes_sam3, nodes_video, nodes_audio, nodes_textgen, nodes_trellis2, nodes_triposplat, and nodes_depth_anything_3. A new extra file does nothing until it is added to that list.

init_builtin_api_nodes globs comfy_api_nodes/nodes_*.py. Present packs include Ideogram, BFL, Gemini, OpenAI, Kling, Luma, Runway, Veo, Wan, Hunyuan3D, ElevenLabs, and others. --disable-api-nodes skips that import and installs a CSP middleware that blocks the frontend from calling the network.

KSampler.sample calls common_ksampler, which calls comfy.sample.sample. Sampler names include euler, euler_ancestral, dpmpp_2m, dpmpp_3m_sde, lcm, ddpm, ddim, and uni_pc. Schedulers are simple, sgm_uniform, karras, exponential, ddim_uniform, beta, normal, linear_quadratic, and kl_optimal.

The HTTP surface in PromptServer includes GET /ws, GET /, GET /embeddings, GET /models, GET /models/{folder}, GET /extensions, POST /upload/image, POST /upload/mask, GET /view, GET /view_metadata/{folder_name}, GET /system_stats, GET /features, GET /prompt, GET /object_info, GET /object_info/{node_class}, GET /history, GET /queue, POST /prompt, POST /queue, POST /interrupt, POST /free, and POST /history.

Jobs are a view over the same in-memory queue: GET /api/jobs filters by status, workflow_id, sort, limit, and offset; GET /api/jobs/{job_id} fetches one; POST /api/jobs/{job_id}/cancel and POST /api/jobs/cancel interrupt a running prompt or dequeue a pending one. Status strings are pending, in_progress, completed, failed, and cancelled. Job ids must be canonical lowercase UUIDs.

WebSocket /ws assigns a clientId, sends the current queue status, and on the first text frame of type feature_flags stores the client flags and replies with feature_flags.get_server_features. Progress is pushed as JSON progress plus binary preview frames.

With --enable-assets, register_assets_routes mounts /api/assets CRUD, content, tags, from-hash, seed, seed/status, seed/cancel, and prune. The module comment tells custom-node authors the assets API is not stable.

UserManager serves GET/POST /users and userdata file APIs. Without --multi-user the only user is default. With --multi-user the user id is the comfy-user request header, checked against user/users.json. Names starting with __ are rejected as system users.

SubgraphManager GET /global_subgraphs and GET /global_subgraphs/{id} merge custom-node subgraphs with every JSON file in blueprints/. CustomNodeManager GET /workflow_templates and GET /i18n expose example workflows and locale JSON shipped inside custom node folders.

ModelFileManager adds experimental listings at GET /experiment/models, GET /experiment/models/{folder}, and GET /experiment/models/preview/{folder}/{path_index}/{filename}. These sit beside the older GET /models routes.

InternalRoutes is mounted at /internal and is documented as frontend-only: GET /logs, GET /logs/raw, PATCH /logs/subscribe, GET /folder_paths, and GET /files/{directory_type} for output, input, or temp.

--list-feature-flags prints CLI_FEATURE_FLAG_REGISTRY and exits before the server starts. Known flags are show_signin_button, enable_telemetry, and partner_run_gate_enabled. Core flags such as supports_preview_metadata and assets cannot be overwritten from the CLI.

--enable-manager imports the optional comfyui_manager package, runs its prestartup, and can block custom nodes via should_be_disabled. If the package is missing, the flag is forced off and a pip command is logged.

data_flow.summary: A client posts a prompt dict whose nodes reference class_type keys in NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS. The server validates links, splits secrets out of extra_data, and heap-queues the job. The worker builds a DynamicPrompt, skips nodes whose outputs are still cached, and calls each node's FUNCTION with inputs resolved from upstream outputs. Model weights enter through folder_paths and comfy.sd; tensors stay on the model-management device policy; UI outputs and files are what cross back to the client. The database, when enabled, catalogs files after the fact and is not on the sampling path.

claims.claim: POST /prompt reads JSON, runs trigger_on_prompt, accepts an optional client prompt_id only if validate_job_id accepts it, and otherwise mints a uuid4. partial_execution_targets limits which nodes are executed.

Before queueing, node_replace_manager.apply_replacements rewrites class_types that are missing from NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS when a NodeReplace mapping was registered. Then execution.validate_prompt returns validity, error, outputs_to_execute, and node_errors.

SENSITIVE_EXTRA_DATA_KEYS are auth_token_comfy_org and api_key_comfy_org. post_prompt pops them into a side channel so they are not stored in the history copy. prompt_worker copies them back into extra_data only for the duration of PromptExecutor.execute.

PromptQueue.put heap-pushes (number, prompt_id, prompt, extra_data, outputs_to_execute, sensitive). A negative number, set when the client passes front, runs the job first. get() moves the item into currently_running under a lock.

execute_async wraps the run in torch.inference_mode, builds DynamicPrompt, resets progress, and sets an IsChangedCache. CacheType defaults to RAM_PRESSURE unless --cache-classic, --cache-lru N, or --cache-none is set.

execution.execute resolves inputs with get_input_data, instantiates the node class into the object cache, honors check_lazy_status by returning PENDING, then get_output_data calls the node FUNCTION. Subgraph outputs and pending asyncio tasks also return PENDING and are resumed on a later turn.

A typical text-to-image node chain is CheckpointLoaderSimple.load_checkpoint to CLIPTextEncode to EmptyLatentImage to KSampler.sample to VAEDecode to SaveImage.save_images. KSampler does not load weights itself.

load_checkpoint_guess_config reads the state dict with comfy.utils.load_torch_file, detects the UNet via model_config_from_unet, picks unet dtype with model_management.unet_dtype, builds the model, and wraps it in CoreModelPatcher or ModelPatcher. CLIP and VAE are split out of the same checkpoint when present.

comfy.sample.sample builds comfy.samplers.KSampler and calls sampler.sample. That path prepares a CFGGuider and runs WrapperExecutor over outer_sample so model_options wrappers can intercept the denoise loop. The returned latent is moved to intermediate_device and intermediate_dtype.

SaveImage writes PNG files under folder_paths.get_output_directory using get_save_image_path. Unless --disable-metadata, the PNG text chunks store the prompt JSON and extra_pnginfo. The node returns a ui.images list of filename, subfolder, and type, which the executor sends as an executed websocket event.

On success, history_result holds ui outputs and meta. PromptQueue.task_done stores that under history[prompt_id] and drops the oldest entry once length exceeds MAXIMUM_HISTORY_SIZE of 10000. Nothing in task_done writes the history to disk.

When assets are enabled, register_executed_outputs catalogs output files during the node, and prompt_worker calls asset_manager.queue_output_scan after GC so the seeder walks the output root. Uploads through /upload/image also call asset_manager.register_upload.

Hidden node inputs such as PROMPT and EXTRA_PNGINFO are filled from the prompt extra_data inside get_input_data. API nodes read auth_token_comfy_org and api_key_comfy_org from the V3 hidden inputs and send them only on requests to the Comfy API base URL.

GET /view resolves a filename inside input, output, or temp, or a blake3: hash via resolve_hash_to_path. Dangerous content types are forced to an attachment octet-stream unless the request is an image-dest SVG.

behavior_traces.summary: Three flows cover how a process comes up, how one prompt becomes pixels, and how results are kept. Startup is single-threaded until the worker thread and the aiohttp loop split. The prompt path is a queue handoff from the event loop into that worker, which then runs the graph asynchronously inside asyncio.run. Persistence is split: pixels and metadata go to the output directory immediately, the job record stays in RAM, and the SQLite catalog is a best-effort index that can be rebuilt by scanning.

claims.claim: Startup step 1: main sets HF_HUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY and DO_NOT_TRACK, imports cuda_malloc, and on Windows with no device override sets CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0. It then may call comfy_aimdo.control.init before torch is imported.

Startup step 2: apply_custom_paths loads extra_model_paths.yaml and every --extra-model-paths-config file through utils.extra_config.load_extra_path_config, then applies --output-directory, --input-directory, and --user-directory onto folder_paths.

Startup step 3: execute_prestartup_script walks each custom_nodes directory and execs prestartup_script.py via importlib, skipping .disabled folders and anything outside --whitelist-custom-nodes when --disable-all-custom-nodes is set.

Startup step 4: start_comfyui builds PromptServer, calls hook_breaker_ac10a0.save_functions, then asyncio_loop.run_until_complete(nodes.init_extra_nodes). That awaits init_public_apis, init_builtin_extra_nodes, init_builtin_api_nodes unless disabled, and init_external_custom_nodes. Functions are restored afterward and cuDNN benchmark policy is reapplied.

Startup step 5: setup_database calls init_db and asset_manager.startup when SQLAlchemy imports. A locked database exits the process if --enable-assets is set. add_routes, hijack_progress, and the prompt_worker thread follow. --quick-test-for-ci then exits 0 before listen.

Startup step 6: start_all awaits prompt_server.setup, which opens an aiohttp ClientSession with no total timeout, then run gathers start_multi_address and publish_loop. --auto-launch opens a browser. On KeyboardInterrupt the finally block calls asset_manager.shutdown.

Prompt step 1: post_prompt logs 'got prompt', assigns the queue number, validates the prompt id, applies node replacements, and awaits validate_prompt. Invalid prompts return HTTP 400 with error and node_errors and are not queued.

Prompt step 2: prompt_worker blocks on PromptQueue.get, pauses the asset scanner, and calls PromptExecutor.execute, which is a synchronous asyncio.run of execute_async. On completion it task_done's the history, sends executing with node null, and may gc.collect plus soft_empty_cache.

Prompt step 3: execute_async emits execution_start, notifies cache providers via on_prompt_start, marks cached nodes with execution_cached, and loops ExecutionList.stage_node_execution until the list is empty or a node returns FAILURE. Success emits execution_success.

Prompt step 4 for sampling: KSampler.sample calls common_ksampler, which builds noise with comfy.sample.prepare_noise, optionally applies latent noise_mask, then comfy.sample.sample. The latent preview callback is latent_preview.prepare_callback, which reaches the progress hook installed by hijack_progress.

Interrupt path: POST /interrupt calls nodes.interrupt_processing. If a prompt_id is supplied it interrupts only when that id is in the running queue. POST /api/jobs/{job_id}/cancel uses PromptQueue.interrupt_if_running under the queue mutex so a late cancel cannot hit the next job. execute_async clears the flag at the start of every prompt.

Persistence path for an image: SaveImage.save_images computes the output path, encodes the tensor to uint8, writes a PNG, and returns ui images. The executor stores that in history. GET /history and GET /view read it back. Restarting the process drops history because it lives only on PromptQueue.

Persistence path for the asset catalog: setup_database migrates SQLite, AssetsEnabled.startup records hash-mode intent, and later scans roots models, input, and output. Migration 0007_record_content_split drops the old asset tables and tells the operator that tags, metadata, and job links were discarded. A pre-upgrade copy is kept at the .bkp path when that revision runs.

testing_signals.summary: pytest is the only test runner. pytest.ini collects tests and tests-unit, adds the repo root to pythonpath, and defines inference and execution markers. tests-unit is large and CPU-oriented, with deep coverage of the asset catalog, path security, and pieces of execution. tests/execution boots a real server graph with testing nodes. Pixel-level inference tests are documented but not wired into the PR workflow, and the GPU workflow CI is manual or label-gated.

claims.claim: pytest.ini sets testpaths to tests and tests-unit, addopts -s, and markers inference and execution so those can be deselected.

tests-unit/README.md says install tests-unit/requirements.txt and run pytest tests-unit/. tests/README.md says inference tests need pytest, websocket-client==1.6.1, opencv-python==4.6.0.66, and scikit-image==0.21.0, then pytest tests/inference.

tests-unit/assets_test covers ingest, scanning, tags, hashing, uploads, and API routes. tests-unit/app_test covers user manager, database locking, and Alembic migrations including migration 0007. tests-unit/execution_test covers the execution list, cache providers, and nested loops. tests-unit/comfy_test covers model detection and folder paths.

tests-unit/security_test holds regression tests named for path traversal and userdata XSS: test_ghsa_779p_02_preview_traversal.py through test_ghsa_779p_06_inline_svg_image_dest.py. folder_paths_test and prompt_server_test cover system-user path blocking.

tests/execution contains test_execution.py, test_async_nodes.py, test_jobs.py, test_preview_method.py, test_progress_isolation.py, and test_public_api.py, plus a testing_nodes pack that is loaded as custom nodes during the run.

test-execution.yml runs on push and pull_request to main, master, and release/**. It installs CPU torch plus requirements.txt and tests-unit/requirements.txt on Python 3.12 and runs python -m pytest tests/execution --skip-timing-checks. The job sets continue-on-error true on ubuntu-latest, windows-latest, and macos-latest.

test-ci.yml is workflow_dispatch only. The push trigger is commented out. It calls comfy-org/comfy-action on self-hosted Linux for Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12 with stable torch, plus a nightly job, using secrets.GCS_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON.

pullrequest-ci-run.yml runs the same GPU action only when a pull_request_target is labeled Run-CI-Test, with use_prior_commit true, across macOS, Linux, and Windows and Python 3.9 through 3.12. It comments a link to ci.comfy.org.

comfy_api_nodes unit coverage is narrow: tests-unit/comfy_api_nodes_test has audio and image conversion tests, a cloud test, and a Gemini response-image test. Most partner node HTTP clients have no unit test in that directory.
Model forward tests that do exist under tests-unit/comfy_test are concentrated on SeedVR2, SenseNova, MiniMax H3, and a VAE tiled-decode case, not on the full ldm family under comfy/ldm.

risk_map.summary: The published threat model is a localhost process whose operator trusts everyone who can reach the port and trusts every installed custom node. The dangerous edges are the unauthenticated HTTP API if --listen is opened, arbitrary code execution from custom nodes, partner-node credential handling, and file serving from output and userdata. Several guards exist and are regression-tested. The queue is volatile, the asset migration 0007 is destructive, and execution CI is allowed to fail without failing the check.

claims.claim: SECURITY.md states the server binds to 127.0.0.1 by default, custom nodes are arbitrary Python and out of vulnerability scope, and bugs that require --listen or a non-default exposure are not treated as vulnerabilities. Reports go to GitHub private advisories.

There is no session, password, or token check on PromptServer routes. --multi-user only trusts the comfy-user header against users.json. Anyone who can reach the port can queue prompts and read output files.

load_custom_node and execute_prestartup_script both exec_module whatever Python is on disk under the custom_nodes folders. That is the intended extension mechanism and also remote-code-execution if an attacker can write those files or if the user installs an untrusted pack.

When --listen is passed with no address it binds 0.0.0.0 and ::. --enable-cors-header replaces the origin check with an explicit CORS middleware that reflects the given origin, or * if the flag is bare. The default middleware is create_origin_only_middleware, which 403s cross-site Sec-Fetch-Site and mismatched Host versus Origin on loopback.

API credentials travel in prompt extra_data. They are stripped before history is stored, but they are present in the worker and are attached as Authorization Bearer or X-API-KEY by get_auth_header. default_base_url is --comfy-api-base, default https://api.comfy.org.

File serving is contained by is_within_directory and realpath, by rejecting leading slashes and .. in /view, and by forcing HTML, JS, CSS, SVG, and XML content types to download. tests-unit/security_test locks those behaviors in. Upload paths also reject commonpath escapes.

GET /internal/folder_paths returns every configured model directory, and GET /internal/logs returns recent log lines. They share the same unauthenticated app as the public routes, mounted as a subapp at /internal.

Alembic revision 0007_record_content_split drops asset tables and deletes tags with no data migration. db.py warns at startup when that revision is applied and keeps the previous file as a .bkp backup.

PromptQueue.history and the pending heap are process memory. A crash or restart loses queued and completed job records even though PNG files remain on disk. Two processes on one database file fail the filelock and, with --enable-assets, exit.

FrontendManager.init_frontend_unsafe, when --front-end-version is not the built-in default, GETs the GitHub releases API and downloads a zip into the custom frontends directory. The default path does not download; it uses the installed pip package.

Checkpoint and .pt loading goes through comfy.utils.load_torch_file. SECURITY.md explicitly declines torch.load issues on PyTorch versions older than what the project ships. supported_pt_extensions includes .ckpt, .pt, .pt2, .bin, .pth, .safetensors, .pkl, and .sft.

test-execution.yml continue-on-error true means a failing tests/execution job does not fail the GitHub check. Combined with test-ci being manual, graph regressions can merge without a required GPU or even a required CPU execution signal.

app/database/models.py still says the ORM models belong there but defines only Base. The real tables are Asset, AssetContent, AssetMeta, AssetTag, Tag, and AssetSystemState in app/assets/database/models.py. Agents that edit the empty module will not change the catalog.

extension_points.summary: New behavior is expected to arrive as a node class, not as a new server route. V1 packs export NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS. V3 packs export an async comfy_entrypoint that returns a ComfyExtension. Built-in extras are an allowlist; API nodes are a filename glob; third-party nodes are whatever sits in the custom_nodes folders. Smaller hooks exist for path config, node replacements, feature flags, cache providers, and the versioned comfy_api facade.

claims.claim: load_custom_node accepts either a module-level NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS dict or a callable comfy_entrypoint. V3 nodes are registered under schema.node_id from GET_SCHEMA. Core names passed in the ignore set cannot be overwritten by later packs.
comfy_extras/nodes_flux.py is the V3 shape: async def comfy_entrypoint returns a FluxExtension. init_builtin_extra_nodes is the registration allowlist for that directory.

Third-party nodes live in folders registered under folder_paths custom_nodes, defaulting to <base>/custom_nodes. A directory named with a .disabled suffix is skipped. prestartup_script.py runs earlier than node import. custom_nodes/example_node.py.example is the in-repo sample.

A custom node can serve static JS by setting WEB_DIRECTORY, or by declaring tool.comfy.web in pyproject.toml, which config_parser.extract_node_configuration reads. Both paths fill nodes.EXTENSION_WEB_DIRS, and the server mounts them at /extensions/<name>.

extra_model_paths.yaml maps folder keys such as checkpoints, loras, and diffusion_models onto extra directories. load_extra_path_config calls folder_paths.add_model_folder_path. is_default inserts the path at the front of the search list.

Node authors register replacements through ComfyAPI_latest.NodeReplacement.register, which calls PromptServer.instance.node_replace_manager.register. apply_replacements only rewrites nodes whose class_type is absent from NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS.

Public Python API versions are registered in comfy_api/version_list.py as ComfyAPI_latest, ComfyAPIAdapter_v0_0_2, and ComfyAPIAdapter_v0_0_1. init_public_apis wraps each in ComfyAPIWithVersion. The latest class exposes execution.set_progress, caching, and node replacement.

comfy_execution.cache_provider.register_cache_provider adds a CacheProvider. PromptExecutor._notify_prompt_lifecycle calls on_prompt_start and on_prompt_end when any provider is registered. Output caches are built with enable_providers=True.

CLI feature flags are added by extending CLI_FEATURE_FLAG_REGISTRY. --feature-flag KEY=VALUE is parsed in _parse_cli_feature_flags and merged into SERVER_FEATURE_FLAGS unless the key is already a core flag.

New partner nodes are picked up automatically if the file matches comfy_api_nodes/nodes_*.py and exports NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS or comfy_entrypoint. HTTP calls are supposed to go through comfy_api_nodes.util.client.ApiEndpoint and sync_op, which attach auth, idempotency, and polling.

Reusable workflow JSON dropped into blueprints/*.json is loaded by SubgraphManager.get_blueprint_subgraphs and served from GET /global_subgraphs without a code change. Custom-node example_workflows directories are a second source.

script_examples/basic_api_example.py and websockets_api_example.py are the supported external-client samples. They post the same prompt payload the frontend posts, including the optional api_key_comfy_org extra_data field.

agent_handoff.summary: Edit the narrowest owner. Nodes and model math do not belong in server.py, and workflow or user ids do not belong in execution.py. Read AGENTS.md before any core change: it bans new network calls, new inference-mode wrappers, new dependencies, and silent dtype fallbacks. Preserve node class names and the prompt JSON shape. Run the unit tests that sit next to the code you touched, and do not assume the GPU workflow CI will catch a regression.

claims.claim: AGENTS.md is the engineering contract: smallest diff, no new dependencies, no core internet calls, no torch.no_grad or torch.inference_mode additions, no model freeze toggles, operations is never None, and model detection must only use the first linear-weight dimension.

An agent changing the prompt lifecycle should read server.py post_prompt, execution.py PromptExecutor.execute_async and execution.execute, and main.py prompt_worker, in that order. Do not thread workflow ids or frontend ids into execution.py.

An agent adding a built-in node should copy a nearby comfy_extras module and append its filename to init_builtin_extra_nodes. Putting the file in the directory alone does not load it. V3 nodes use comfy_entrypoint and io.ComfyNode rather than a new NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS entry in nodes.py.

An agent changing checkpoint loading should start at CheckpointLoaderSimple.load_checkpoint, then comfy.sd.load_state_dict_guess_config and model_detection.model_config_from_unet. Do not add a model-specific branch to a shared helper when only one caller needs it.

Path and file changes must keep using folder_paths.get_full_path, get_annotated_filepath, and is_within_directory. Combo widget values are not a security boundary. System user directories use the __ prefix and get_public_user_directory returns None for them.

Do not add a second place that stores auth_token_comfy_org or api_key_comfy_org. The strip list is SENSITIVE_EXTRA_DATA_KEYS. History and /queue responses must keep going through the sensitive-key removal.

The asset HTTP API is explicitly unstable. app/assets/api/routes.py tells custom-node authors not to depend on it. Schema changes also require an Alembic revision under alembic_db/versions, and revision 0007 already discarded catalog data once.

Torch must not be imported before the warning in main.py around the 'Main code' section. Custom nodes that import torch at module import are tolerated later, but core import order before that line is a known footgun.

execute_async already enters torch.inference_mode for the whole prompt. Adding another inference-mode wrapper inside a model or node violates AGENTS.md and can break any training or gradient path that temporarily disables the global mode.

After a node-execution change, run pytest tests-unit/execution_test and, if the public prompt or jobs contract moved, pytest tests/execution. Asset changes should run pytest tests-unit/assets_test and tests-unit/app_test. Path changes should run tests-unit/security_test and tests-unit/folder_paths_test.

init_external_custom_nodes inserts the comfy/ directory at the front of sys.path so old custom nodes can import helpers unqualified. Renaming a module that those nodes import as a bare name will break packs that are not in this repo.

Windows startup forces CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 unless --cuda-device, --default-device, or the env var is already set. A change that assumes multi-GPU visibility on Windows by default will not match what users actually run.

report.agent_prompt:
You are working in ComfyUI core, version 0.37.0, declared in pyproject.toml and mirrored by comfyui_version.py. It is a local node-graph runtime for diffusion, video, audio, and 3D models, plus an aiohttp server. It is not the desktop shell and not the frontend SPA. Those live in other repositories. This process starts at main.py. start_comfyui builds server.PromptServer, loads nodes, optionally opens SQLite, and starts a daemon prompt_worker over execution.PromptQueue. The default bind is 127.0.0.1 port 8188.

Read AGENTS.md before editing. Then read the file you will change and its callers. For queue or HTTP work read server.py post_prompt and execution.py PromptExecutor.execute_async plus execution.execute. For a built-in node read nodes.py load_custom_node and the init_builtin_extra_nodes allowlist. A file dropped into comfy_extras is not loaded unless that list names it. V3 nodes export async comfy_entrypoint and return a ComfyExtension, as comfy_extras/nodes_flux.py does. For checkpoints read CheckpointLoaderSimple, comfy/sd.py load_checkpoint_guess_config, and comfy/model_detection.py. For sampling read nodes.common_ksampler, comfy/sample.py sample, and comfy/samplers.py. For paths read folder_paths.py. For the asset catalog read app/assets and alembic_db. Treat app/assets/api/routes.py as unstable: the file says custom nodes must not depend on it.

Rules that are enforced here: keep execution.py free of workflow ids, frontend ids, and persistence bookkeeping. Do not add torch.inference_mode or torch.no_grad. execute_async already wraps the whole prompt in torch.inference_mode. Do not add freeze or unfreeze helpers. Do not add outbound network calls to core. Partner HTTP belongs only in comfy_api_nodes and is skipped when --disable-api-nodes is set. Model __init__ operations is never None. Model-detection code may use only the first dimension of a linear weight. Do not add convenience dtype casts in model forward. Do not add a dependency unless the change cannot work without it. Preserve existing node class names and the prompt JSON shape.

Prompt path: POST /prompt, also mounted at /api/prompt, validates with execution.validate_prompt, strips auth_token_comfy_org and api_key_comfy_org into a side channel listed in SENSITIVE_EXTRA_DATA_KEYS, and heap-pushes the job. The worker calls PromptExecutor.execute, which is asyncio.run of execute_async. That walks a comfy_execution.graph.DynamicPrompt and calls execution.execute per node. Lazy nodes return PENDING. Subgraph expansions add ephemeral nodes. The default cache is RAM_PRESSURE, overridable with --cache-classic, --cache-lru, or --cache-none. History is an in-memory dict capped at 10000 entries. It is not the database. Restarting the process drops the queue and history. Images land on disk through SaveImage into the output directory, with PNG prompt metadata unless --disable-metadata.

--enable-assets turns on the SQLite catalog at user/comfyui.db, migrated by Alembic. Head revision 0007_record_content_split drops the previous asset tables on purpose. Do not write a migration that silently destroys user tags again. Two processes must not share one database file. init_db takes a non-blocking filelock and exits when --enable-assets cannot get it.

Security assumptions from SECURITY.md: localhost by default, every client who can reach the URL is trusted, and custom nodes are arbitrary Python. load_custom_node and prestartup_script.py exec user code. Do not weaken folder_paths.is_within_directory, the /view content-type attachment logic, or UserManager path checks. Multi-user mode is the comfy-user header plus user/users.json, not authentication. System user ids are prefixed with __. Do not log or persist API keys. They are removed before history is stored and must stay removed.

Tests use pytest, with pythonpath set to the repo root. Fast checks are pytest tests-unit. Graph behavior is pytest tests/execution, which is what .github/workflows/test-execution.yml runs on CPU torch. That workflow sets continue-on-error, so a red job may not fail the check. tests/inference needs real models and is not the PR unit job. The full GPU workflow is comfy-org/comfy-action, triggered manually or by the Run-CI-Test label. After a node-execution change run tests-unit/execution_test. After an asset change run tests-unit/assets_test and tests-unit/app_test. After a path change run tests-unit/security_test.

Traps: do not import torch before the guard in main.py. On Windows, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES is forced to 0 unless the user opted out. init_external_custom_nodes inserts the comfy directory at the front of sys.path, so bare import names are a compatibility surface. Node replacements apply only when the old class_type is missing from NODE_CLASS_MAPPINGS. Dynamic VRAM swaps in ModelPatcherDynamic only when comfy-aimdo initializes. Keep diffs narrow and match the style of the file you edit.
